identity.author: John Davenant
identity.work: Two Dissertations (De praedestinatione through Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol)
identity.edition: Dissertationes duae (Cambridge: Roger Daniel, 1650). Partial through Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol (baptism). Cap. IX Arg. 12 prayers remain.

scope.locus: De praedestinatione Cap. IX Arg. 11 Baptism / Corvinus + Sol.
scope.next_locus: Cap. IX Arg. 12 (public prayers / confidence that the Word profits all hearers).

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 11 (Corvinus): absolute predestination/reprobation makes baptism of many infants, by God's first intention, useless and sealing nothing — without the infants' fault
english: Those who set predestination and reprobation as hanging absolutely on God's freest will — not on foreseen faith and unbelief of the predestined and reprobate — make baptism administered to many infants useless by God's first intention, and sealing nothing, and that without fault in the infants who receive it. For if we set many infants of the faithful as precisely reprobated, it is most certain that baptism seals nothing for them.
sections.latin: Qui ponunt praedestinationem et reprobationem ex liberrima Dei voluntate absolute pendentem, et non ex praevisa fide et infidelitate praedestinatorum et reprobatorum, illi faciunt Baptismum circa multos infantes administratum, ex prima Dei intentione statui inutilem, et nihil obsignare, idque citra culpam infantium quibus administratur. Nam si ponamus multos infantes fidelium praecise reprobatos, nihil ipsis per Baptismum obsignari certissimum est.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: absolute predestination/reprobation defined — decree to lead some by special grace to glory, deny that preparing mercy to others, and punish for final guilt of sin
english: The absolute predestination and reprobation we affirm depends on God's freest will. It means nothing other than his eternal decree. By that decree, of mere good pleasure and supreme mercy, he established to lead some infallibly to glory through the means of special grace. To others, of mere liberty of will, he denies that supreme mercy which prepares special grace. That denial presupposed, God sees them finally bound by sin's guilt, and decrees them punished for that guilt.
sections.latin: Praedestinatio et reprobatio illa absoluta, quam nos a liberrima Dei voluntate dependere asserimus, nil aliud designat quam aeternum illud Dei decretum, quo statuit pro mero suo beneplacito, et ex summa misericordia, quosdam per specialis gratiae media ad gloriam infallibiliter perducere, aliisque pro mera libertate voluntatis suae hanc summam misericordiam specialis gratiae praeparatricem denegare, qua negatione praesupposita, Deus videt eosdem reatu peccati finaliter constringendos, et propter eundem reatum decernit puniendos.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: why baptism more useless on our view than theirs? — they also grant eternal damnation of reprobates, church-born baptism by command, and reprobation before birth
english: That premised, I ask why baptism of many infants is called useless and sealing nothing on our view rather than on theirs. Because God from all eternity decreed to damn the reprobate? They dare not deny that. Because reprobation by decree and baptism by command clash? They too grant that all born in the Church must be baptized by God's command, and that many of them were nonetheless reprobated by his eternal decree before they were born. Or because they teach damnation fixed in God's eternal, certain, infallible knowledge, whereby as before his eyes he saw a man bound by sin's guilt? We profess the same.
sections.latin: Hoc praemisso, quaero cur ex nostra sententia Baptismus circa multos infantes administratus inutilis statuatur, et nihil obsignare, potius quam ex sententia adversariorum. An quia Deo decretum est ab omni aeternitate damnare reprobatos? At hoc ipsi non audent negare. An quia Reprobari ex decreto Dei et Baptizari ex mandato Dei sibi adversentur? At ipsi etiam agnoscunt omnes in Ecclesia natos ex mandato Dei baptizandos, et multos horum nihilominus aeterno Dei decreto fuisse reprobatos antequam nascerentur. An denique quia illi damnationem infixam docent aeternae, certae et infallibili notitiae Dei, qua veluti ante oculos cernebat hominem peccati reatu constrictum? At nos etiam idem profitemur.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: remaining charge — special grace prepared for some only makes baptism useless for the rest; we deny the consequence
english: So only this remains: because we say special grace that in fact leads to glory is prepared and given to some of God's mere good pleasure, and to others neither prepared nor given, we are judged to make baptism altogether useless for these latter. We deny that consequence.
sections.latin: Illud igitur unum reliquum est, ut quia nos dicimus specialem gratiam, et de facto ad gloriam perducentem quibusdam ex mero Dei beneplacito praeparari et donari, aliis nec praeparari nec donari, idcirco judicemur statuere Baptismum quoad hosce posteriores prorsus inutilem. Nos negamus hanc consequentiam.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: baptism seals as Arminians allow — original-sin remission for every infant; actual-sin remission and regeneration for believers when adult
english: And we can say no less than the Arminians themselves. Baptism seals to every infant the remission of original sin, by which alone infant age is held. It also seals remission of actual sins prepared in Christ's blood for those who repent and believe when they come to adulthood and fall into actual sins. It seals, further, regeneration and renewal wrought from the incorruptible seed of word and Spirit in all believers, once they live to an age capable of the divine word.
sections.latin: Et dicere possumus non minus quam ipsi Arminiani, Baptismum obsignare cuivis infanti originalis peccati remissionem, quo solo tenetur aetas infantilis; obsignare etiam actualium peccatorum remissionem in Christi sanguine paratam resipiscentibus et credentibus, cum ad aetatem adultam pervenerint, et in actualia inciderint; obsignare etiam regenerationem et innovationem ex incorruptibili semine verbi Spiritusque efficiendam in omnibus credentibus, postquam ad aetatem verbi Divini capacem vixerint.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: Augustine, Prosper, Council of Valence on original-sin remission; baptism seals new-covenant remission of actual sins for the whole course of life (1 John i. 9)
english: On remission of original sin Augustine agrees everywhere (De pecc. mer. et remiss. 1.28 and 2.4). Prosper also, ad Cap. Gall. Resp. 2, embraces the same view. Finally the Council of Valence, cap. 5, proposes this as to be held most firmly. Likewise for remission of actual sins under the new covenant's condition: that is sealed most firmly to every baptized person — not only at the moment of receiving baptism, but for the rest of life's course. Whoever is baptized into the name of Jesus Christ, if he sins after baptism, has in that same Christ's blood, through faith, expiation of his sins prepared (1 John i. 9).
sections.latin: De remissione peccati originalis habemus Augustinum ubique adstipulantem: De pecc. mer. et remiss. lib. 1. cap. 28. et lib. 2. cap. 4. Prosper etiam ad Cap. Gall. Resp. 2. eandem sententiam amplexatur. Denique, in Concilio Valentino, cap. 5. hoc firmissime tenendum proponitur. Porro, de remissione peccatorum actualium, sub conditione novi foederis impetranda, idem statuendum est: Hoc enim firmissime omni baptizato obsignatur, non solum quoad ipsum momentum quando Baptismum suscipit, sed quoad reliquum cursum vitae suae. Nam quicunque baptizatus est in nomen Jesu Christi, ille si post Baptismum peccaverit, in sanguine ejusdem Christi paratam habet per fidem peccatorum suorum expiationem; 1 Joann. i. 9.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 11 Sol: Augustine on sacrament preceding heart-conversion; Fulgentius — baptism suffices for infants while reason is incapable; Aquinas — Christ's passion applied by the sacrament
english: Finally, on adults' actual renewal or regeneration — when by the power of divine word and Spirit one is converted and by believing justified — Augustine writes: In baptized infants the sacrament of regeneration precedes, and if they hold Christian piety, conversion of heart also follows, whose mystery preceded in the body (lib. 4 Contra Donatist. cap. 24). So of all baptized infants we assert with Fulgentius: The sacrament of faith, which is holy baptism, while infants' age cannot be capable of reason, suffices them for salvation (De fid. ad Petrum Diac. cap. 30). Nor do we scorn Aquinas on this: Infants who have nothing whereby they can turn themselves to the justifying cause have that cause itself — Christ's passion — applied to them through the sacrament of baptism (Quaest. disp. de Justific. art. 3).
sections.latin: Denique, de renovatione sive regeneratione actuali adultorum, quae fit cum quis virtute verbi Divini Spiritusque convertitur, et credendo justificatur, sic scribit Augustinus, In baptizatis infantibus praecedit regenerationis sacramentum, et si Christianam pietatem tenuerint, sequitur etiam in corde conversio, cujus mysterium praecessit in corpore, lib. 4. Contra Donatist. cap. 24. Nos itaque de omnibus infantibus baptizatis cum Fulgentio asserimus, Sacramentum fidei, quod est sanctum baptisma, quamdiu rationis aetas infantium capax esse non potest, sufficit eis ad salutem, De fid. ad Petrum Diac. cap. 30. Neque Aquinatis hac de re dictum adspernamur; Qui, inquit, non habent infantes unde possint se convertere ad causam justificantem, ipse causa justificans, scilicet passio Christi, applicatur eis per sacramentum baptismi, Quaest. disp. de Justific. art. 3.
